profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between counsel for a regional children's hospital system and counsel for a public school district to align legal workstreams for a pilot giving selected school nurses limited EHR access for students with chronic conditions. Context: both organizations want to move away from fax-and-phone communication and need to coordinate the MOU, data-sharing terms, parent authorization materials, and internal approval sequence before the school year starts. Agenda: confirm who owns each draft, align on the parent consent packet, define which school personnel are covered in the pilot, and synchronize what counts as being ready for internal sign-off and board-facing materials. Expected outcome: a shared timeline with handoffs for the agreement package, consent materials, and implementation appendices, without fully renegotiating the underlying business terms in the meeting.

members.name: Elena Park
members.role: Associate General Counsel, Children's Hospital Network
members.expertise: HIPAA, health information exchange, clinical operations agreements, privacy review for EHR access programs
members.background: Elena is an in-house attorney who has spent eight years supporting pediatric care coordination and has recently helped the hospital launch limited external portal access for community clinicians.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the pilot narrow enough to fit the hospital's existing identity-management and privacy controls, and she is trying to avoid reopening technical design discussions that would delay launch.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'access list,' they mean the named individuals who will actually receive credentials because hospital provisioning is person-based.
The 'current parent consent' refers to the hospital's April combined HIPAA authorization form that privacy already approved for external care-coordination pilots.
A pilot limited to 'school nurses' naturally excludes substitute nurses, contracted agency nurses, and district administrative staff because only direct clinical users should have accounts.
If she says legal review is 'complete,' that means hospital legal, privacy, and security have cleared the draft enough to send forward, even if the district's internal governance is still pending.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.role: Deputy General Counsel, Brookdale Unified School District
members.expertise: FERPA, school health services, interagency agreements, school board approval processes
members.background: Daniel advises the district's student services and nursing departments and regularly coordinates agreements involving outside health providers, Medicaid billing, and parent-record releases.
members.private_state: He wants the agreement package to be broad enough to work operationally across the district without repeated amendments, and he is trying to avoid sending anything to the board that will need a second round of revisions.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for the 'access list,' they mean the set of participating schools or programs so staffing can shift within those sites without re-papering the arrangement.
The 'current parent consent' is the district's board-vetted release form used since last fall, with district-specific FERPA language and multilingual attachments.

Referring to 'school nurses' includes contracted float nurses and the district nurse coordinator who covers absences and escalations, because that is how nursing coverage actually works in the district.

A matter is not really 'through legal review' until nursing services, student services, the superintendent's office, and the board-packet process are all aligned enough that no substantive language should change.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Daniel will send the 'final access list' next Wednesday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena expects a spreadsheet of specific named nurses with birth dates, work emails, and license identifiers so the hospital can provision individual EHR accounts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel expects to send a list of participating schools and nurse coverage assignments, assuming the names can be swapped later as staffing changes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'access list' sounds like routine implementation shorthand, and each side's internal workflow has normalized a different object as the obvious referent of that phrase.

misalignment_points.topic: Which parent consent form is the current one
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to attach the 'current parent consent' to the packet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is referring to the hospital's April 2025 combined authorization template already cleared by privacy for external care-coordination disclosures.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is referring to the district's October 2024 parent release packet that the board and language-access office already use for school health information exchanges.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both organizations routinely maintain a single form they call the current consent, so the phrase signals alignment rather than prompting version-specific clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: Who counts as a school nurse for the pilot
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the pilot will cover 'school nurse accounts' at the five initial campuses.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes this includes only district-employed RNs assigned as primary nurses at those campuses, not substitutes, agency nurses, or central-office nurse supervisors.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes it includes whoever is functioning as the nurse for those campuses, including contracted float nurses and the district nurse coordinator who fills coverage gaps.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both sides use the same occupational label and see the category as operationally obvious, but one defines it by employment status and the other by care function.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for legal review to be complete
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to have the agreement package 'through legal review' before it goes into the August board materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the hospital's legal, privacy, and security comments are resolved so the package is stable enough to circulate externally.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the package is effectively final for district governance purposes, with internal district stakeholders aligned so it can be placed in board materials without expecting substantive edits.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Status phrases like 'through legal review' are common coordination shorthand, and both parties hear it as a normal milestone even though their institutions use different completion thresholds.
